The gpt-6-sol design consult challenged the premise: at the current tip the worker create detaches the core-session build and its prewarm (create.rs:649-665), TS never awaited the prewarm, and the ledger's '+310-315 response' was an INFERENCE from the TUI's worker-direct-connect timestamp, never a direct observation. Prediction if the consult is right: all three show the kernel is ALREADY off the create/ready path; the ~250ms paint->ready is the durable-write fan-out + process chain + attach/mount tail, with probe quantization ~0.

outcome: measured - THE ATTRIBUTION CORRECTION (an honest negative for the proposed kernel-gate cut)
decision: THE KERNEL GATE IS ALREADY OFF THE CREATE/READY PATH AT THE CURRENT TIP - the cut proposed from the 20261001-031500 ledger is DEAD, and this record is the measurement-honest correction. (1) CAUSAL: the kd discriminator (the identical payload, every kernel-python exec +500ms via the PRIME_AGENT_KERNEL_PYTHON wrapper) leaves fresh-cold ready unchanged (tip p50 311.25 vs kd p50 308.91, delta -2.34ms, bands fully overlapping) while every kd trial provably has NO kernel python in existence at ready (sighting 0/10, py CPU 0.0 - the exec is blocked behind the sleep-wrapped probes; every tip trial sights it 10/10 at ~150-205ms with first CPU ~198). (2) REMOVAL: the np probe (prewarm Some(false), 0/10 kernel spawns confirmed by the 15s census) moves ready +12.1ms inside a deep window's own +-150ms noise. (3) DIRECT: the full-tree wire census observes the create request, the kernel python's exec MID-create-RTT (concurrent, not awaited), the create response, the worker direct connect (+~2ms), the attach over the worker socket (+~5-11ms), and ready - in every trial the response/attach/ready sequence proceeds on its own schedule; the prior ledger's 'response gates on the kernel's readiness' was an inference from the TUI's worker-direct-connect timestamp in a connects-only strace parse (the no--f blindspot: only the main thread is traced, the tokio threads' socket I/O is invisible) - now replaced by the direct observation. THE CORRECTED DECOMPOSITION of the fresh-cold ready (~306-312ms p50 class): the create+attach round trips over the durable-write fan-out (the sibling fanout lane's surface) + the process chain (exec->daemon 6-12ms; daemon->bind ~40-50ms incl. the supervisor-config fresh-fsync; bind->worker 5-11ms; worker spawn->bind ~1ms) + the attach (~4-11ms) + the mount tail (~13-23ms healthy); probe quantization ~0 on fresh legs (input_buffered 10/10 - the echo IS the mount render); THE KERNEL SHARE IS ZERO. THE FIRST-TOUCH ORACLE at this tip: NO shared join - ensure() CONSUMES the startup JoinHandle; concurrent first-touch callers either both see startup=None and double-spawn interpreters, or arrive mid-boot and get a bare 'kernel startup failed'; the open #3257 (shared watch, both reviewers expecting APPROVE at the amended head 7ddb838a4) is exactly this fix and this record cross-confirms its base-side finding. PIVOT CANDIDATES RELAYED to the stopgate-hardening lane (both confirmed live on main at 3358e0016, both persisting at #3257's head): (a) kill-during-boot: kill() is synchronous, takes only an ALREADY-PUBLISHED manager - a kill before publication returns while the boot completes and leaves a resident kernel; (b) the dispose check/publish TOCTOU: run_startup checks raced_dispose in one lock scope and publishes state.manager in a LATER lock scope - a dispose landing between leaks a live manager into a disposed provisioner. No PR: the lane is a measurement correction; the shared-startup fix ships through #3257 and the gaps through the stopgate-hardening lane.
